summary: Guidance requested: separate rate buckets for interactive microservices and long-running background multiplexers
description: Issue summary: BrightCart is seeing intermittent 429s that correlate with a new microservice deployment which multiplexes many short interactive chat requests alongside periodic background embedding flushers. They want a recommended configuration to avoid cross-talk between background worker bursts and low-latency front-end calls. Impact: customer-facing chat sessions occasionally receive 429s for 10-30s windows during nightly batch flushes, causing degraded end-user experience and increased client retries. Environment: production, dedicated pool in us-east-1. Request: best-practice configuration for separate burst pools/priority lanes, recommended token-bucket sizing, backoff/timeout settings in SDK, and console alerts to monitor for repeat regressions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy microservice A (interactive chat) and B (background embed flusher) behind same API key. 2) Start both with typical production concurrency (A: ~120 concurrent short calls; B: 8 parallel background workers performing 3k small-embed calls each). 3) Observe 429s surfacing on interactive calls within 30s of worker flush start. 4) Check console token consumption and see background bursts consuming majority of tenant burst credits.

customer_notes: Customer message: "Since we moved to a microservice pattern the chat team complains about occasional 429s during our embed flush. We use a shared API key and short-lived service tokens for workers. Is there a way to carve the quota so interactive calls never see worker noise?"

investigation_notes: Checked console: burst_pool consumption spikes aligned with cron jobs from embed flusher service. Tenant-level burst credits were being drawn by non-priority routes.
Verified background workers used ephemeral short-lived tokens generated from shared API key; this caused token bucket accounting to aggregate under tenant key instead of route-level buckets.
Hypothesis: default route weight and lack of route-isolation allow background flushers to drain shared burst credits before refill windows, producing soft 429 windows for low-latency calls.

Ran staging test with route-config: set routeWeight(interactive)=0.8, routeWeight(background)=0.2 and enabled isolatedBurstPool=true for /v1/generate. Interactive path maintained <60ms p95 while background throughput was limited as configured.

Suggested SDK change: ensure worker processes use a distinct API key or scoped route (recommended: create a background-service scoped API key with dedicated burst pool), and set exponential backoff with jitter: initial=200ms, factor=2, max=10s.
proposed_mitigation: 1) Create separate API keys or scoped routes for interactive vs background services so quota accounting occurs independently. 2) In Console, enable ‘isolatedBurstPool’ on interactive routes and set routeWeight to favor low-latency lanes. 3) Reserve a small continuous token allocation for interactive route (sustained quota) plus a limited burst credit for background workers. 4) Tune worker concurrency and batching (increase batch size to reduce per-request tokens). 5) Apply SDK retry policy with exponential backoff and jitter for background flushers. 6) Add alerting on Console: 'interactive-429-rate > 0.5% for 2m' and dashboard for burst_pool consumption.
resolution: Provided step-by-step configuration and tested recipe. Customer validated fix in staging: interactive 429s stopped under equivalent background load. Recommended production rollout plan: 1) Create background-scoped API key; 2) Apply isolated burst pools to interactive routes in Console; 3) Deploy workers with new key and reduced concurrency; 4) Observe for 24h and escalate if any residual 429 windows. Ticket closed after customer confirmed success in prod rollout.
follow_up_actions: Add an internal runbook snippet to Console docs that outlines 'separating burst pools for mixed-latency traffic'
